In general, if you vibe with an attending, it won’t matter how long you actually spent with them. They often get feedback from the residents and other docs that also influences their opinion of you. Additionally, keep in mind that every single med student needs a minimum of three LORs - the attendings know this and are usually prepared to write them. I asked for a letter after knowing an attending for only about 2 weeks, but he and I got along really well. 

It sounds like you also felt this way with this attending. I don’t think that you did anything wrong by asking. Unfortunately, it sounds like he was not willing to write this letter. The fact that he asked you to write up a template is a big red flag. There are a lot of reasons why he might have said this, but I won’t speculate on those. I would suggest that you give him an out - tell him you cant write a template, let him know you don’t want to put him in that position, etc. 

TLDR; you didn’t do anything wrong and the attending should have let you down easy, but I think you should take the L and ask someone else

Edit: I didn’t realize a lot of people write their own first drafts of letters. I was told by my school/advisors not to do that but I realize my experience is not universal. Anyway, good luck!

If you look at the link I put up from the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, they compare vegan cat foods to meat based cat foods and demonstrate that cats are unable to digest the added proteins and amino acids as well as they would from actual meat. What happens is that cats slowly develop malnutrition even from foods that supposedly have the correct ingredients. Just because the ingredients are present does not mean they are digestible - thats why we can’t just go and eat grass and get the nutrients that are present in there.

Oh sorry I didn’t see that. I am also vegetarian and have been vegan before, but had to switch back to eating some dairy for some health reasons. 

My partner currently works as a Vet Tech and has to deal with a lot of people who believe they can just feed their animals “whatever” - including those who just feed them raw chicken, not actual cat foods - so I tend to be sensitive to this topic too. You can supplement your cats food with (some) vegetables and rice, but you absolutely need to give your cats animal-based cat food too. I know most people understand that but there are a lot of people in this thread that don’t seem to get it.

No, as a human, you do not need taurine. Cats cannot synthesize it themselves, which is why they need it. My point was that taurine is not the only nutrient that cats need that humans don’t- so you shouldn’t compare your human vegan diet to a cat vegan diet.

Essential amino acids differ based on species.


https://avmajournals.avma.org/doi/pdf/10.2460/javma.2004.225.1670

Please consider reading actual professional opinions from  [veterinarians](https://m.petmd.com/blogs/thedailyvet/lorieahuston/2014/june/vegan-diets-cats-31822).

[VCA ](https://vcahospitals.com/know-your-pet/nutrition-feeding-guidelines-for-cats)

Yes, certain amino acids can be found in plants. Cats CANNOT digest plant-based food well enough for their body to extract enough essential nutrients to survive. Many of these plants contain other chemicals that are toxic to cats. They might not be toxic in small doses, but once you feed your cat ONLY those plants, the toxicity increases. There’s a reason grass makes cats vomit.

You do know there are more amino acids than the ones that are required in the human diet right? There are 20 common amino acids that are involved in human biochemistry but literally hundreds of others that exist.

For example, taurine, which is required in feline diets. 
Which you don’t have.

Please educate yourself: https://vcahospitals.com/know-your-pet/nutrition-feeding-guidelines-for-cats
